title: Are the Democrats going to save us this time?
gist: Noah Smith argues the usual American release valve of voting out a bad Republican party is losing power, because the Democratic Party's ascendant DSA faction — exemplified by Wisconsin gubernatorial nominee Francesca Hong and Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed — brings its own anti-NATO, fiscally loose and anti-data-center agenda. He notes Trump's approval broke its assumed 40% floor while MAGA hardens into a transferable ideology, leaving both parties as sources of policy risk.

insights.claim: Trump's approval rating broke through the 40% floor that many analysts assumed existed, according to Nate Silver's tracking.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: A broken approval floor changes midterm base rates and the probability distribution for 2026 congressional control.
insights.quote: Some people thought Donald Trump’s approval rating would have a floor around 40%. Well, it didn’t

insights.claim: MAGA is transitioning from a personality cult into a durable, transferable ideology defined by xenophobia, economic retrogression and the belief that wealth made the West immoral and weak.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: If the ideology outlives the man, post-Trump policy risk (tariffs, immigration, alliance decay) does not mean-revert after 2028.
insights.quote: MAGA is already morphing from a personality cult into an ideology — a deeply xenophobic, economically retrograde ideology obsessed with expelling immigrants, and convinced that wealth has made the West immoral and weak.

insights.claim: A Manhattan Institute poll found 25 percent of Republicans under 50 self-identified as holding antisemitic views and 31 percent as holding racist ones, alongside documented 'groyper' infiltration of GOP staff ranks.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Quantifies radicalization of the GOP's future staff pipeline — a structural, not cyclical, input to long-run U.S. political risk.
insights.quote: A Manhattan Institute poll found that a full 25 percent of Republicans under 50 self-identified as having antisemitic views, and 31 percent as holding racist ones
insights.locator: GOP veterans fret about the rising generation

insights.claim: Election denial has become a litmus test in the GOP, with a negligible number of Republicans willing to publicly affirm the 2020 election's legitimacy and denial serving as a fast track to prominence.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Institutional acceptance of election results is itself now a variable; that is a tail risk that markets historically do not price for the U.S.
insights.quote: The number of Republicans who will declare in public, in no uncertain terms, that the 2020 election was legitimate is now negligible.

themes.theme: Diminishing returns to 'throw the bums out'

insights.claim: Successive Democratic corrective waves have shown diminishing returns: Obama delivered effective anti-recessionary macro policy plus health and finance reform, while Biden's industrial policy came bundled with fiscal profligacy that fed inflation and left the debt unaddressed.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: The democratic self-correction mechanism is degrading, which weakens the standard assumption that U.S. policy errors are self-limiting over an election cycle.
insights.quote: Biden gave us the return of industrial policy, but his fiscal profligacy — often squandered on things like student debt forgiveness and subsidies for already-overpriced service industries — contributed to inflation
insights.locator: I think if you look at those episodes

insights.claim: The author still unambiguously endorses voting Democratic in 2026 for congressional checks on lawlessness, corruption and Ukraine policy, while arguing the upside from doing so is smaller than in past cycles.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: A divided-government 2027 is the realistic base case being argued for — relevant for fiscal, tariff and Ukraine-aid expectations.
insights.locator: And we should elect Democrats, this November

insights.claim: Because the release valve of simply replacing incumbents no longer suffices, fixing U.S. governance now requires something beyond electoral alternation.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: The core investable claim: assume persistent U.S. policy volatility across administrations rather than reversion to a competent center.
insights.quote: If the U.S. is going to turn its problems around, “throw the bums out” is no longer enough.
insights.locator: I still think the choice of which party

insights.claim: DSA member Francesca Hong is all but certain to be the Democratic nominee for governor of Wisconsin, marking the faction's breakout from deep-blue cities into statewide races.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Statewide DSA nominations are the leading indicator that left-faction policy preferences will shape the next Democratic administration's agenda.
insights.locator: Let’s look at the type of candidates

insights.claim: The hope that a class-focused socialist faction would shed 2010s culture-war baggage has failed, because the DSA candidates are proving to be the most culturally left of all.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Kills the 'economically populist but culturally moderate left' thesis that some analysts use to forecast Democratic electability.
insights.quote: the DSA types are the wokest of the woke.
insights.locator: Some had hoped that the Democrats’ socialist faction

insights.claim: Prediction markets on Kalshi immediately discounted Hong's general-election chances after her refusal to recant an anti-Thanksgiving position, and Bernie Sanders signaled he would not endorse her.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Real-money markets are repricing left-faction candidates' general-election viability in real time — a tradable read on Democratic seat expectations.
insights.quote: prediction markets immediately began to discount Hong’s chances of beating her Republican opponent in the fall
insights.locator: Hong backtracked a couple of days later

insights.claim: Abdul El-Sayed won the Michigan Senate primary but by a closer-than-expected margin with very little working-class support, indicating the left's advance costs the party political capital rather than expanding its coalition.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Weak working-class support for left candidates undercuts the realignment narrative and points to Democratic underperformance in Senate races.
insights.quote: El-Sayed just won his primary for the Michigan Senate race, but a closer-than-expected election, with very little working-class support

insights.claim: Democrats are spending accumulated political capital moving left instead of converting anti-Trump alienation into a durable majority, leaving the median voter in disgusted ambivalence between two extremes.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Predicts continued narrow, unstable majorities and policy whiplash rather than a stable governing coalition in either party.
insights.quote: Democrats have spent their political capital moving to the left.
insights.locator: This demonstrates exactly what I mean

insights.claim: A leftist is unlikely to win the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, but the eventual nominee will probably concede substantial policy priorities to the ascendant DSA faction, as Biden did for Sanders supporters on student debt.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: The practical forecast: expect DSA-flavored policy riders inside a nominally moderate 2028 platform — concessions, not capture.
insights.locator: It’s doubtful that a leftist candidate will win

themes.theme: Policy consequences of a leftward Democratic Party

insights.claim: A DSA-influenced administration is unlikely to restore the liberal alliance system, since the faction blamed the U.S. and NATO for Russia's invasion of Ukraine and called for NATO withdrawal.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Alliance-decay risk is bipartisan, not Trump-specific — relevant to European defense spending and transatlantic security premia through 2028 and beyond.
insights.quote: Recall that the DSA blamed the United States and NATO for Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, and called for withdrawal from NATO.
insights.locator: But on foreign policy in general

insights.claim: DSA economic policy could look more Trumpian than expected: professed free-trade positions are driven by negative polarization against Trump's tariffs, while the underlying impulse toward labor protection and command-and-control would likely reassert itself.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Do not assume a Democratic win removes trade-restriction risk; the tariff regime may prove structurally bipartisan.
insights.locator: On economic policy, too, a DSA administration

insights.claim: The national debt is framed as the country's biggest looming economic threat, and the DSA faction is explicitly not a balanced-budget constituency — illustrated by Hong campaigning to cut property taxes by 44%.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Fiscal deterioration has no political constituency in either party, supporting a structurally steeper long end and persistent term-premium risk.
insights.quote: Remember that Francesca Hong wants to cut property taxes by 44%.

insights.claim: Trump has deliberately avoided interfering with the AI buildout, which the author identifies as the force keeping the economy afloat, whereas the DSA and many progressive Democrats want to halt data center construction.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Makes AI capex an explicit partisan variable: a Democratic administration influenced by the left is a direct policy risk to the single largest growth driver.
insights.quote: Trump has hurt the economy in some ways, but he has always been very careful not to mess with the AI buildout — the force that’s keeping the economy afloat.
insights.locator: And where the DSA would break from Trumponomics

insights.claim: Halting data center construction would remove the U.S. economy's biggest tailwind, and it is now positioned as the more reasonable of a leading Democratic nominee's platform planks.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Anti-data-center policy is moving from fringe to mainstream Democratic orthodoxy — the key political risk to AI infrastructure and power demand.
insights.quote: her more reasonable position is to ban the single industry that is currently keeping the American economy afloat.
